explanation: Wildcard: matches any subject (as a subject attribute) or any object (as an object attribute).

Directory path. As a subject attribute, matches the process's current working directory; as an object attribute, matches the directory the accessed file is under. Also accepts the built-in aliases execdirs, systemdirs, and untrusted.
MIME type of the file, as fapolicyd's magic-based classifier determines it (e.g. application/x-executable, text/x-shellscript). Check a file's type with fapolicyd-cli --ftype.
Whether the file must be present in the trust database: 1 = trusted (verified against the RPM database or /etc/fapolicyd/fapolicyd.trust), 0 = explicitly not required to be trusted.
Audit login UID (loginuid) of the process — the same immutable auid used throughout the kernel audit subsystem. 4294967295 means unset (no login session).
Real user ID (or account name) of the process.
Real group ID (or group name) of the process.
Audit session ID of the process.
Parent process ID — e.g. used to identify kernel threads such as nfsd (ppid=2, since kernel threads have no executable of their own).
Short command name of the process (as in /proc/<pid>/comm), e.g. dnf, nfsd.
Full path to the process's executable. Supports a glob: prefix for fnmatch-style pattern matching.
Access pattern the kernel identified: normal, ld_so (dynamic-loader-mediated access), ld_preload, or static.
Full path of the file being accessed. Supports a glob: prefix for fnmatch-style pattern matching.
Hash of the file's contents, lowercase, no 0x prefix — matches a specific file by content rather than by path.
